title: Transcend Heavenly Dao
next_chapter_hook: The Founder's silhouette flickered in the Dimension Turbulence, His voice echoing through eternity: 'Chen Ji, are you prepared to become the new Chess Player?'

text.content: The moment the residual soul dissolved, the warmth in Chen Ji's palm vanished. That thread of bloodline power he thought had long turned cold still left scalding warmth between his fingers. 'This time, let me save you.' His voice was soft—a vow whispered to himself, a final promise to someone who could no longer hear. The surrounding Void trembled slightly as the Tianji Record Fragment turned pages on its own, and ancient runes that had never before appeared slowly coalesced on the yellowed surface. Mo Xiansheng had said that when the first volume's objective was completed, the second page would unseal—but what emerged was not the anticipated martial technique, but coordinates pointing to the deepest chamber of the Tianji Pavilion.

Chen Ji traversed the Void following those coordinates, each step landing on the cracks of destiny. The core area of the Tianji Pavilion was entirely different from what he had seen before—no gilded palaces, no neatly arranged archives of jade slips, only a heart-piercing void. In the pure darkness, stars were born and destroyed at visible speeds, time losing all meaning here. A pressure beyond comprehension surged from all directions, as if the entire universe's weight pressed upon his shoulders. This was the aura of transcending Heavenly Dao—Chen Ji's pupils constricted. He finally understood that the enemy he faced was far more terrifying than he had imagined.

In the depths of the Void, a pair of eyes slowly opened. Those eyes had no physical form to support them, their pupils swirling with the birth and death of billions of stars, as if the entire universe were but a mote of dust within them. The way it regarded Chen Ji was like a human looking down at an ant beneath its feet—not arrogance, but something beyond arrogance, a tranquility, because to Him, whether Chen Ji existed or not made no essential difference. 'You have finally arrived.' The voice did not come from those eyes, but rang directly in Chen Ji's Mental Sea, each word carrying weight enough to make the soul tremble.

dialogue.content: 'The moment you stepped in here, I knew everything—including the fragment of the Tianji Record in your body, all your machinations over these years, and... your missing sister.' The owner of those eyes manifested in complete form, no longer a虚幻 projection, but a truly embodied existence. His face was too blurred to remember, but the Laws flowing around Him continuously reshaped the surrounding space, each thread of Dao韵 exceeding anything Chen Ji had ever witnessed. 'The Tianji Pavilion is not the legacy you believed it to be. It is me—or rather, we—the seed planted eons ago.'

text.content: Chen Ji's heart skipped a beat. The Tianji Pavilion was a seed? He forcefully suppressed the surging waves of shock, his expression remaining as calm as still water, only the white-knuckled fists betraying him. The Founder seemed satisfied with his reaction, continuing: 'The Eye of Heavenly Dao is not the 'antagonist' you understand. It is the Rule, the Order, the necessity that maintains this realm's operation.' The Founder's form paced slowly through the Void, each step shattering a dimension, 'And what I desire is to transcend all of this—to break this solidified cycle, allowing possibility to bloom anew. Thus I need a chess piece, one capable of reaching the final game.'

dialogue.content: 'Eons ago, I selected the first chess piece.' The Founder's voice carried a trace of reminiscence. 'That brilliant genius exhausted his entire life pursuing the path to transcend Heavenly Dao, yet ultimately turned to ash beneath the Heavenly Tribulation.' Chen Ji's breath hitched—he recognized the shadow of that story. 'After that, I selected many more. Each reached heights you cannot imagine, yet failed at the crucial moment.' The Founder's gaze refocused on Chen Ji. 'Until you appeared. Do you know why I chose you? A servant disciple of the Tianqing Sect, atrash mocked by all?'

text.content: Chen Ji did not answer. Of course he knew the answer—the Tianji Record had chosen him, or rather, bypassed all geniuses and selected atrash. He had always believed this was mere random coincidence, a joke of destiny. But standing before the Founder now, he suddenly understood. The Tianji Record had not chosen him—it had bypassed everyone. 'Because you were weak enough.' The Founder spoke the cruel truth. 'Weak enough to pose no threat. Weak enough to escape Heavenly Dao's notice. Weak enough to hide until today.' The Founder's voice carried a hint of appreciation. 'Walking the world as atrash, weaving a chess game none could break—this is precisely what I wished to see.'

dialogue.content: 'The page of Tianji Record in your body is a gift I specially left for you.' The Founder's smile was clearly visible to Chen Ji—the satisfaction of a hunter watching prey step into a trap. 'It grants you the ability to foresee the future, yet consumes your Heavenly Fate Value with each use. You thought this was a curse? No, this is selection. The day your Heavenly Fate Value is exhausted is the moment you become the 'Chess Game Terminator.' Then, you will possess sufficient power—and sufficient desperate resolve.' The Founder's form suddenly pressed closer, His pressure collapsing like a mountain. 'And now, I need to know: are you ready?'

text.content: Chen Ji felt that unimaginable pressure, his internal organs trembling. Cold sweat dripped from his temples, but his gaze became unprecedentedly clear at this moment. He thought of Mo Xiansheng, the old man who had guarded the Tianji Record for countless years as a residual soul. Was Mo Xiansheng a chess piece of the Founder? Or... another existence unwilling to be manipulated? He thought of his sister Chen Nian, those eyes always blurred in the Tianji Record's visions. If he accepted this fate, what would happen to Chen Nian? If he refused, what would occur? Only the being calling himself the Founder seemed to know the answer.

choice.prompt: Facing the Founder's question, Chen Ji needed to respond. He could rage in defiance, feign compliance, or maintain silence. Different choices would determine his first move in this game of destiny.

choices.description: 'Since I'm a chess piece, then what is my sister Chen Nian to you? Was her interference with Tianji Record's visions also within your calculations?'
choices.visible_cost: May provoke the Founder, losing part of the intelligence source
choices.visible_reward: May obtain crucial information about Chen Nian
choices.risk_hint: The Founder's attitude will determine the subsequent plot direction

text.content: Chen Ji slowly raised his head; in those eyes, usually calm as stagnant water, dangerous light now burned. 'Since I'm a chess piece, then what is my sister Chen Nian to you? Was her interference with Tianji Record's visions also within your calculations?' His voice was not loud, yet carried blade-sharp edge. The Founder fell silent for a moment—that silence itself was an answer. 'She is the variable I left for you, the... accident I left for this chess game.' The Founder's tone finally shifted subtly. 'I thought she would become your weakness, causing you to make wrong choices at critical moments. But I didn't expect you to resist the Tianji Record's temptation, not burning through your Heavenly Fate Value early to save her.'

choices.description: 'Become a Chess Player? Sounds tempting. But do I have the right to refuse? In this chess game, what autonomy can I actually gain?'
choices.visible_cost: May be seen as willing submission, losing the Founder's重视 for one's abilities
choices.visible_reward: Gain more information about the chess game's rules
choices.risk_hint: The Founder may therefore underestimate you, lowering your status in subsequent cooperation

text.content: A slight smile curved Chen Ji's lips—the perfect expression of greed and ambition. 'Become a Chess Player? Sounds tempting.' He spoke slowly, his tone carrying deliberate eagerness, 'But do I have the right to refuse? In this chess game, what autonomy can I actually gain?' The Founder's eyes narrowed slightly, seemingly scrutinizing Chen Ji's true thoughts. After a moment, He laughed—that laughter echoed through Dimension Turbulence, carrying wisdom that saw through everything. 'You're more interesting than I anticipated. Don't worry, I won't force a choice from you now. After all... the chess game has just begun, and there is much you still need to learn.'

choices.description: I don't need to know your plans. I only need to know one thing—how to make your entire chess game collapse?
choices.visible_cost: May immediately enter direct conflict with the Founder
choices.visible_reward: Test the Founder's true attitude and bottom line
choices.risk_hint: The Founder may display power beyond imagination

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly laughed—a completely unrestrained laugh, carrying the madness and pride finally released after years of suppression. 'I don't need to know your plans.' His voice echoed through Dimension Turbulence, colliding head-on with the Founder's pressure, 'I only need to know one thing—how to make your entire chess game collapse?' The Founder's expression changed for the first time. That was not anger, nor surprise, but... gratification? 'Excellent.' He said. 'This is the reaction I wanted to see. If you had obediently accepted fate, I would have doubted my own choice.' The Founder's Laws began to fluctuate violently. 'Since you possess such resolve, let me tell you—the true chess game has just begun.'

The Founder waved His hand, and a massive chessboard suddenly materialized in the Dimension Turbulence. That chessboard was woven from countless points of light, each point a person's destiny trajectory—Chen Ji saw Ling Yuan, Han Lie, Su Qingyao, even Chen Nian in the Holy Sect in the distance. 'This is the chess game I have arranged.' The Founder's voice carried a certain sacred solemnity. 'And you are the only piece on this board capable of reaching the endgame. But remember—' His gaze sharpened abruptly, 'You are both a piece and part of the chess game. Every choice you make reshapes the entire board.'

dialogue.content: 'Do you know why the Tianji Record shows you exactly three hours into the future?' The Founder suddenly asked, His tone carrying a hint of amusement. Chen Ji did not answer, but his gaze turned dangerous. 'Because three hours is precisely enough for you to change one thing, yet insufficient to see the full picture.' The Founder laughed. 'Every foresight is purchasing an incomplete map with your Heavenly Fate Value. You think you're laying out a strategy, but every move you make fills gaps in my plans. This is the essence of the Tianji Record—it is the hand of the guide, and also the chain of the enslaver.'

choice.prompt: The Founder revealed the true nature of the Tianji Record, and Chen Ji needed to decide how to cope with the impact of this revelation.

choices.description: If the Tianji Record is a chain, then its incompleteness is also part of your plan. Why would you make your most important chess piece incomplete?
choices.visible_cost: May touch upon core secrets the Founder is unwilling to reveal
choices.visible_reward: Obtain clues about the complete form of the Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: The Founder may therefore retract some information

text.content: A cold smile curled on Chen Ji's lips. 'If the Tianji Record is a chain, then its incompleteness is also part of your plan?' He paced slowly, each word like a poisoned needle. 'Why would you make your most important chess piece incomplete?' The Founder's eyes narrowed—this was the first time He showed genuine wariness. 'A good question.' He fell silent for a moment. 'Because a complete Tianji Record is too powerful—powerful enough that even I cannot control it. What I need is a chess piece capable of reaching the endgame, not an existence capable of replacing me.' Chen Ji's heart一震—So that was it. The incompleteness of the Tianji Record was not a mistake, but a limitation.

choices.description: Then let me thank you for your 'kindness.' Granting me the ability to change destiny, yet making me pay the price with each use—this is the most sophisticated control technique.
choices.visible_reward: Make the Founder take your independent consciousness more seriously
choices.risk_hint: May affect the difficulty of obtaining resources later

text.content: Chen Ji laughed coldly, that smile carrying undisguised mockery. 'Then let me thank you for your 'kindness'.' He spoke word by word. 'Granting me the ability to change destiny, yet making me pay the price with each use. Heavenly Fate Value, foresight time limits, the incomplete Tianji Record... each is a chain, each is control. This is the most sophisticated ruling technique—making you think you're resisting, when you've never escaped the palm.' The Founder did not deny, instead nodding. 'You're very clever—clever enough to worry me at times. But these are the rules. A chess piece without chains is too dangerous, and I... am not yet prepared.'

The Founder suddenly extended His hand, pointing to a light on the chessboard—that spot displayed Chen Nian's figure. She was trapped in a cage woven from countless runes, eyes closed, surrounded by aura of the same origin as the Tianji Record. 'Her name is Heavenly Fate Lock Key.' The Founder's voice carried no emotion. 'When your Heavenly Fate Value is exhausted and you're about to become the Chess Game Terminator, she is your final... insurance.' Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply, a murderous intent unprecedented burst from within him. 'What do you intend to do with her?' His voice was dangerously low. 'Do?' The Founder laughed. 'Make her your new chain, or... make you willingly become my replacement.'

dialogue.content: 'Chen Ji, you are my most perfect creation in hundreds of millions of years.' The Founder's voice suddenly softened, carrying a twisted tenderness. 'You are clever enough, patient enough, ruthless enough. You could maintain your own plans while everyone mocked you, rise again after every failure. You... are my chosen one.' His gaze pierced through Dimension Turbulence,直视ing Chen Ji's eyes. 'But precisely because of this, when you finally rebel against me, it will become the most magnificent finale. I have waited for this day for a very long time.' The Founder's form began to fade, but before completely disappearing, He left one final sentence: 'When we meet again, I hope you can give me a surprise—not like those previous chess pieces, disappointing me.'

text.content: The Founder's form completely dissolved, leaving only Chen Ji standing alone in the Dimension Turbulence. The lights on the chessboard still slowly circulated; those lights representing the destiny trajectories of those close to him now appeared so dazzling. The Tianji Record Fragment in his arms pulsed warmly, as if responding to something. He looked down at his palm, where the warmth remained from when the residual soul dissolved. 'This time, let me save you.' He repeated his own words, his voice carrying a certain determination. The Founder called him a chess piece, but the most dangerous thing in a chess game is precisely those unwilling to be manipulated. Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze penetrating Dimension Turbulence, looking into the depths of that Void. The true chess game has just begun. And he had already decided his next move.

In the depths of the Void, the Founder's voice rang like eternal echoes once more, no longer carrying the lofty pressure from before, but gaining an inexplicable undertone: 'Chen Ji, are you prepared to become the new Chess Player?' These words echoed through Dimension Turbulence, each word like a brand seared into Chen Ji's Mental Sea. The Tianji Record Fragment suddenly trembled violently, and ancient text never before seen appeared on the yellowed surface—content Mo Xiansheng had never mentioned, seemingly only appearing when facing the Founder. Chen Ji lowered his head to凝视 those characters, and in the depths of his eyes, dangerous light ignited. He knew that from this moment, his life would completely change—not because destiny was fated, but because he finally saw how heavy the chains he needed to break truly were.
